cases.sentence: В ___ на Варварке, внизу которого был питейный дом, слышались пьяные крики и песни.
cases.explain: «недостроенном доме» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: From an unfinished house on the Varvárka, the ground floor of which was a dramshop, came drunken shouts and songs. On benches round the tables in a dirty little room sat some ten factory hands. Tipsy and perspiring, with dim eyes and wide-open mouths, they were all laboriously singing some song or other. They were singing discordantly, arduously, and with great effort, evidently not because they wished to sing, but because they wanted to show they were drunk and on a spree. One, a tall, fair-haired lad in a clean blue coat, was standing over the others. His face with its fine straight nose would have been handsome had it not been for his thin, compressed, twitching lips and dull, gloomy, fixed eyes. Evidently possessed by some idea, he stood over those who were singing, and solemnly and jerkily flourished above their heads his white arm with the sleeve turned up to the elbow, trying unnaturally to spread out his dirty fingers. The sleeve of his coat kept slipping down and he always carefully rolled it up again with his left hand, as if it were most important that the sinewy white arm he was flourishing should be bare. In the midst of the song cries were heard, and fighting and blows in the passage and porch. The tall lad waved his arm.

cases.sentence: Все они пьяные, потные, с ___, напруживаясь и широко разевая рты, пели какую-то песню.
cases.explain: «мутными глазами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.

cases.sentence: ___ рвался в дверь, грудью наваливаясь на целовальника.
cases.explain: «Другой кузнец» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Another smith tried to enter the doorway, pressing against the publican with his chest.

cases.sentence: В это время ___ поднялся с земли, и расцарапывая кровь на разбитом лице, закричал плачущим голосом:
cases.explain: «первый кузнец» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: At that moment the first smith got up and, scratching his bruised face to make it bleed, shouted in a tearful voice: “Police! Murder! … They’ve killed a man, lads!”

cases.explain: «соседних ворот» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Oh, gracious me, a man beaten to death—killed! …” screamed a woman coming out of a gate close by. A crowd gathered round the bloodstained smith.

cases.translation: “Come along then! Come along then!” the publican and the tall young fellow repeated one after the other, and they moved up the street together. The bloodstained smith went beside them. The factory hands and others followed behind, talking and shouting.

cases.sentence: У угла Маросейки, против большого с запертыми ставнями дома, на котором была вывеска ___, стояли с унылыми лицами человек двадцать сапожников, худых, истомленных людей в халатах и оборванных чуйках.
cases.explain: «сапожного мастера» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: At the corner of the Moroséyka, opposite a large house with closed shutters and bearing a bootmaker’s signboard, stood a score of thin, worn-out, gloomy-faced bootmakers, wearing overalls and long tattered coats.
